title: KL10 engineering evidence hierarchy
summary: Use primary DEC architecture and production microcode to decide machine semantics; use TOPS-20 source to decide what the guest intended; use reference emulators as implementation evidence rather than architectural authority.
procedure: Identify the exact machine question: instruction semantics, paging, interrupt/APR behavior, I/O channel behavior, or guest policy.
Consult DEC processor/technical documentation for the architectural contract.
For microcoded edge cases, inspect production KL10 Model-B microcode before generalizing from another simulator.
Use TOPS-20 V7 monitor/BOOT/POSTLD source to establish what the guest is deliberately doing at the observed PC.
Only then compare Cornwell/SIMH or other emulator implementations for a practical implementation model.
Replay from the last qualified checkpoint and reject any downstream state whose upstream machine history is architecturally impossible.
Open kl10.current-continuation before resuming the live TOPS-20 line so stale downstream fixtures are not mistaken for qualified state.
invariants: A reference emulator is not the architecture specification.
An APR condition bit, page-fail word, and CPU-visible cycle outcome are distinct evidence.
Extended-section control flow must preserve the full 30-bit PC where the Model-B architecture requires it.
Installed physical memory capacity is a machine property; sparse host storage must not silently create nonexistent guest core.
Never promote a checkpoint merely because it reaches a familiar address.
